text: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) encodes homologues of human interleukin-10 (hIL-10) that modulate myeloid cells. Monocytes exposed to hIL-10, cmvIL-10 (expressed during productive infection), and LAcmvIL-10 (a differentially spliced form expressed during latent and productive phases) were compared. Within 24 h, hIL-10 and cmvIL-10 upregulated Fcγ receptors, stimulated phagocytosis of IgG-opsonised erythrocytes, and decreased MHC class II (HLA-DR) expression on purified monocytes. In contrast, LAcmvIL-10 reduced HLA-DR only at later times (48 h and 72 h) and did not increase Fcγ receptor expression. The authors conclude that cmvIL-10 promotes monocyte differentiation towards a pro-phagocytic phenotype, whereas LAcmvIL-10 acts via a different mechanism. The significance for HCMV pathogenesis is discussed.
